f3_program: collection("danai.house.decorations", "decoration", "danai.house", source("Danai is decorating her house for Halloween"))
add("put_plastic_skulls", "danai", at("danai.house.decorations.plastic_skulls.count", "current"), 12, source("She puts 12 plastic skulls all around the house"))
observe(at("danai.house.decorations.broomsticks.count", "current"), 4, "count", source("She has 4 broomsticks"))
observe(at("danai.house.decorations.broomsticks.count_per_door_side", "current"), 1, "count_per_door_side", source("1 for each side of the front and back doors to the house"))
add("put_spiderwebs", "danai", at("danai.house.decorations.spiderwebs.count", "current"), 12, source("She puts up 12 spiderwebs around various areas of the house"))

add("put_pumpkins", "danai", at("danai.house.decorations.pumpkins.count", "current"), scale(event_field("put_spiderwebs", "quantity"), 2), source("Danai puts twice as many pumpkins around the house as she put spiderwebs"))
add("place_cauldron", "danai", at("danai.house.decorations.cauldrons.count", "current"), 1, source("She also places a large cauldron on the dining room table"))
observe(at("danai.house.decorations.budgeted_additional.count", "current"), 20, "count", source("has the budget left to buy 20 more decorations"))
observe(at("danai.house.decorations.remaining_to_put_up.count", "current"), 10, "count", source("has 10 left to put up"))
query("value", "danai.house.decorations.total_put_up.count")
assumptions: The singular phrase "a large cauldron" denotes one decoration.
The hypothetical treats the 20 budgeted decorations as intended purchases that will be put up, and the 10 remaining decorations as additional decorations still to be put up.

f3_program: collection("farmer.offspring_pigs", "pig", "farmer", source("A farmer owns a hog that recently gave birth to 6 piglets"))
produce("piglet_birth", "farmer.hog", at("farmer.offspring_pigs.count", "current"), 6, source("a hog that recently gave birth to 6 piglets"))
observe(at("farmer.offspring_pigs.fully_grown.sale_price_per_pig", "current"), 300, "dollar", source("he can sell the fully grown pig for $300"))
observe(at("farmer.offspring_pigs.minimum_growth_duration", "current"), 12, "month", source("Each piglet must grow for at least 12 months before it is large enough to be sold"))
observe(at("farmer.offspring_pigs.feed_cost_per_animal_month", "current"), 10, "dollar", source("It costs the farmer $10 per month to feed each animal until it is sold"))
remove("sell_after_12_months", "farmer", at("farmer.offspring_pigs.count", "after_12_months"), 3, source("the farmer sells 3 pigs after 12 months"))
remove("sell_after_16_months", "farmer", at("farmer.offspring_pigs.count", "after_16_months"), 3, source("the farmer sells 3 pigs after 12 months, and the remaining 3 pigs after 16 months"))
query("value", "farmer.offspring_pigs.total_profit_after_food_cost")
assumptions: The sold pigs are the six piglets after they have grown, and "each animal" refers to each of those offspring until its sale.
The 12-month and 16-month feeding periods are measured from the piglets' birth; the mother hog is excluded because no sale of it is stated.

f3_program: collection("global_gym.cardio_machines", "cardio_machine", "global_gym.gyms", source("A global gym decides to replace all of its cardio machines"))
observe(at("global_gym.gyms.count", "current"), 20, "count", source("They have 20 gyms"))
observe(at("global_gym.cardio_machines.bikes.count_per_gym", "current"), 10, "count_per_gym", source("Each gym has 10 bikes, 5 treadmills, and 5 elliptical machines"))
observe(at("global_gym.cardio_machines.treadmills.count_per_gym", "current"), 5, "count_per_gym", source("Each gym has 10 bikes, 5 treadmills, and 5 elliptical machines"))
observe(at("global_gym.cardio_machines.elliptical_machines.count_per_gym", "current"), 5, "count_per_gym", source("Each gym has 10 bikes, 5 treadmills, and 5 elliptical machines"))
observe(at("global_gym.cardio_machines.bike.unit_cost", "current"), 700, "dollar", source("The bikes cost $700 each"))
percent_more(at("global_gym.cardio_machines.treadmill.unit_cost", "current"), at("global_gym.cardio_machines.bike.unit_cost", "current"), 50, source("The treadmills cost 50% more than that"))

multiple(at("global_gym.cardio_machines.elliptical_machine.unit_cost", "current"), at("global_gym.cardio_machines.treadmill.unit_cost", "current"), 2, source("The elliptical machines are twice as expensive as the treadmills"))
query("value", "global_gym.cardio_machines.total_replacement_cost")
assumptions: Every one of the 20 gyms has the listed machine counts, and each listed machine is replaced once.
"That" in the treadmill-cost statement refers to the $700 cost of one bike.

f3_program: collection("james.sales_visits.houses", "house", "james.sales_visits", source("James visits 20 houses to try and make a sale"))
observe(at("james.sales_visits.houses.count", "day_1"), 20, "count", source("James visits 20 houses to try and make a sale"))
same(at("james.sales_visits.houses_with_sales.count", "day_1"), at("james.sales_visits.houses.count", "day_1"), source("He manages to sell something in every house"))
multiple(at("james.sales_visits.houses.count", "day_2"), at("james.sales_visits.houses.count", "day_1"), 2, source("The next day he visits twice as many houses"))
percent_of(at("james.sales_visits.houses_with_sales.count", "day_2"), at("james.sales_visits.houses.count", "day_2"), 80, source("only sold to 80% of houses"))

remove("day_1_sales", "james", at("james.items.count", "current"), scale(at("james.sales_visits.houses_with_sales.count", "day_1"), 2), source("he sold two things at each house in each of the two days"))

remove("day_2_sales", "james", at("james.items.count", "current"), scale(at("james.sales_visits.houses_with_sales.count", "day_2"), 2), source("he sold two things at each house in each of the two days"))
query("value", "james.items_sold.total_count")
assumptions: The initial visit is day 1 and "the next day" is day 2.
"Each house" in the final condition means each house where James made a sale, so the two-item quantity applies per successful house.

f3_program: observe(at("group.closing_cash", "2019"), 183.2, "million_dollar", cell("Closing cash", "2019"))
observe(at("group.closing_cash", "2018"), 121.6, "million_dollar", cell("Closing cash", "2018"))
observe(at("group.closing_cash.change_percentage", "2019_vs_2018"), 50.7, "percent", cell("Closing cash", "Change (%)"))
query("value", at("group.closing_cash.change_percentage", "2019_vs_2018"))
assumptions: "Change" refers to the table's explicit "Change (%)" column for closing cash, representing the change from 2018 to 2019.
The "$ million" table heading applies to the 2018 and 2019 closing-cash values.
